visual_invariants: PRIMARY: overall size and silhouette are forced by the available front-axle bay volume (wishbones, uprights, steering, crash structure, halfshaft height, cooling/HV corridors) — not a free-form industrial design.
The unit must pack into a compact homologated box on the order of ~259 × 343 × 267 mm (press-derived) and ~32 kg dry — fill the bay, do not float a smaller sculpture inside a huge apron.
Motor + inverter + single-speed reduction + differential are ONE unitised sealed brick (spec kit), denser than a typical open rear manufacturer cradle cassette.
Halfshaft exits at front axle height fix lateral width and case split planes; shaft stubs are mandatory exterior language.
Coolant ports and HV DC connector sit on faces that can reach the front-bay service corridors — bosses are packaging-forced, not decorative.
Public exterior language is a sealed cast/machined housing (often gold-anodised in press photos) — windings and PCB farms are cutaway/ghost only.
Lucid sealed-unit press photography is the FFF training check: if bay + function are understood, morphology should look very similar — never paste proprietary STEP/STL.
Lucid Air road Tech Talk / oil-microjet patents are PHYSICS training for cooling/winding only — different duty and envelope from the race FPK.
Gen3 role is primarily regen; Gen3 Evo adds limited AWD traction windows — morphology still bay-first; do not invent a second remote inverter brick.
Service is whole-unit removal from the front bay: mounts, thermal loops, HV and LV/control — not field-open motor service.
